profit.q: How does Scaliente calculate net profit?
profit.a: Scaliente starts with revenue and reconciles ad spend, product costs, shipping, payment fees, taxes and expenses you declare. Each line item remains visible so you can verify the calculation.

attribution.q: Why can attribution differ from ad platforms?
attribution.a: Each platform applies its own windows and models. Scaliente reconciles first-party signals with the order and keeps direct, unattributed or low-signal sales visible.

pixel.a: Tracking uses Shopify's official Web Pixel extension, running in Shopify's isolated environment. It does not inject a modification into your theme.

seo.title: How to use the ROAS calculator
seo.p1: ROAS (Return on Ad Spend) measures the revenue generated for every unit of currency spent on advertising. A ROAS of 3x means that for every 1 invested in ads, you generate 3 in revenue.
seo.p2: The breakeven ROAS is the minimum ROAS needed to cover all your costs (product, shipping, payment fees) and reach the breakeven point. Below this threshold, every sale loses you money.
seo.p3: POAS (Profit on Ad Spend) goes further by measuring actual profit relative to ad spend. A POAS of 1x means your profit exactly covers your ad spend.

items.title: Last click

items.description: The first and last touchpoints receive more weight than the middle steps.

items.question: What is a Shopify attribution pixel?
items.answer: It is an extension that listens to Shopify journey events, retains available campaign signals and connects them to orders so sales sources can be analysed.

items.question: Does the Scaliente Pixel replace Meta, Google or TikTok pixels?
items.answer: No. It complements advertising integrations: Scaliente builds its own journey view and consolidates performance from the five supported platforms.

items.question: Does the Pixel slow down the store?
items.answer: It runs as a Shopify Web Pixel extension in a sandboxed environment. Sending to the Scaliente collector is asynchronous and designed not to block the storefront.

items.question: When does the data become actionable?
items.answer: Collection begins after installation and does not recreate the past. Scaliente displays coverage and considers the channel view actionable from 60% attributed revenue.

items.question: Which attribution models are available?
items.answer: Last click, last non-direct click, first click, linear, time decay and position-based attribution.

meta.description: What is a Shopify profit tracker, which data should it reconcile and how can you evaluate a reliable net-profit view?

profitTracker.title: What is a Shopify profit tracker?
profitTracker.summary: Understand what a profit tracker calculates, what it cannot infer and how to use it without confusing revenue with profitability.
profitTracker.answer: A Shopify profit tracker reconciles orders with product costs, shipping, fees, taxes and advertising spend to estimate net profit over a selected period.
keyPoints: Shopify revenue is not net profit.
The result depends on complete, accurate costs.
A clear data cadence is more useful than a vague real-time claim.

sections.title: From revenue to net profit
paragraphs: Shopify records sales, refunds and payments. A profit view also needs the variable and fixed costs borne by the store. Missing costs do not disappear economically; they are simply absent from the calculation.
Always read the result with its period, currency and coverage. The tracker is an operating view, not a substitute for statutory accounts.
bullets: Net revenue after discounts and refunds.
COGS, shipping, fees, taxes and ad spend.
Declared expenses and visible assumptions.

sections.title: How to evaluate a profit tracker
paragraphs: A useful tool explains its formula, each data source and refresh cadence. Check how it treats refunds, currencies, pending orders and unattributed sales.
Scaliente receives orders through Shopify webhooks. Spend from five supported ad platforms syncs once or twice daily and can be refreshed manually.
bullets: Ask what is calculated, excluded or estimated.
Check the last sync time for each source.
Prefer visible uncertainty to forced attribution.

sections.title: Turn the dashboard into decisions
paragraphs: Connect every metric to an operating question: did margin fall because of COGS, shipping, discounts or ads? Is ROAS above break-even?
Check missing data, compare equivalent periods and document the action taken.
bullets: Diagnose before changing a budget.
Compare profit, margin and spend over one period.
Share the calculation method with the team.

methodology.title: How Scaliente calculates Shopify profit.
methodology.summary: A readable method showing what enters the calculation, when data is refreshed and what still needs verification.
methodology.answer: Scaliente starts with available Shopify revenue for the period, then deducts available product costs, shipping, fees, taxes, advertising spend and declared expenses.
keyPoints: Each value keeps its source and period.
Orders and ad spend do not share the same cadence.
Missing data must be fixed rather than presented as certainty.

sections.title: The working formula
paragraphs: The operating view starts from observed revenue and subtracts available cost categories. Refunds and order statuses stay separate so collected revenue, refunded revenue and risk are not mixed.
The result depends on store configuration and should be reconciled with accounting for tax or statutory decisions.
bullets: Revenue − COGS − shipping − fees − taxes − ads − expenses.
Use one currency and date window.
Keep refunds and disputes separately visible.

sections.title: Source, cadence and coverage
paragraphs: Orders arrive through Shopify webhooks. Ad spend syncs once or twice daily, with manual refresh available. Exchange rates come from the European Central Bank.
The Web Pixel collects only after activation. Scaliente keeps direct and unattributed sales visible instead of inventing prior history.
bullets: Never claim history the pixel did not observe.
Show last refresh and missing integrations.
Keep unattributed sales in the total.

meta.description: Understand the difference between Shopify revenue, gross margin and net profit before deciding where to invest.

revenueVsProfit.title: Shopify revenue or net profit?
revenueVsProfit.summary: Two stores can report the same revenue and keep very different profit.
revenueVsProfit.answer: Revenue measures sales. Net profit measures what remains after the product, shipping, payment, tax, advertising and other included costs.
keyPoints: Revenue describes sales volume, not retained value.
Gross margin and net profit answer different questions.
Comparisons require the same period and method.

sections.title: Three levels not to confuse
paragraphs: Revenue starts with sales. Gross margin mainly removes product cost. An operating net-profit view includes additional observable costs.
Revenue can rise while profit falls when discounts, ads, shipping or fees rise faster.
bullets: Revenue: sales over the period.
Gross margin: revenue minus product cost.
Net profit: revenue minus included costs.

sections.title: Read a change correctly
paragraphs: Compare equal periods and verify that integrations cover the full window. Then break down the change by cost.
A metric becomes actionable when its movement can be tied to a checkable cause.
bullets: Verify coverage before comparing.
Break down margin instead of reading one total.
Document the change behind the variance.

meta.title: ROAS vs POAS for Shopify | Scaliente
meta.description: Compare ROAS and POAS, understand their formulas and avoid confusing attributed revenue with profit.

roasVsPoas.title: ROAS vs POAS: revenue or profit?
roasVsPoas.summary: ROAS measures revenue attributed to advertising. POAS places ad spend against profit.
roasVsPoas.answer: ROAS divides attributed revenue by ad spend. POAS divides the selected attributable profit by that spend. They are complementary but answer different questions.
keyPoints: High ROAS does not guarantee positive margin.
POAS depends on complete cost data.
State the attribution model before comparing.

sections.title: Two formulas, two views
paragraphs: ROAS compares attributed revenue with budget but ignores product economics.
POAS adds margin. Campaigns with the same ROAS can have different outcomes.
bullets: ROAS = attributed revenue ÷ ad spend.
POAS = attributable profit ÷ ad spend.
State the model and attribution window.

sections.title: Choose the metric for the decision
paragraphs: Use ROAS to read media revenue; add POAS and break-even for margin decisions.
Before cutting a campaign, inspect direct sales, missing signals and conversion delay.
bullets: Media view: ROAS and attributed revenue.
Economic view: POAS, margin and break-even.
Final decision: combine coverage and profit.

meta.title: Break-even ROAS Formula and Shopify Calculator | Scaliente
meta.description: Calculate the minimum ROAS needed to cover costs and understand when a Shopify campaign becomes profitable.

breakevenRoas.title: Calculate your break-even ROAS.
breakevenRoas.summary: Break-even ROAS is the point where revenue exactly covers the costs included in the calculation.
breakevenRoas.answer: When contribution margin is expressed as a share of revenue, break-even ROAS can be estimated as 1 divided by that margin. The margin must already exclude advertising spend.
keyPoints: The threshold depends on accurate costs.
One average can hide product-level differences.
Returns, discounts and taxes move break-even.

sections.title: Build the threshold correctly
paragraphs: Start with expected net revenue and remove variable costs excluding ads. The remaining contribution funds acquisition.
Use separate thresholds when costs differ significantly by product or country.
bullets: Use revenue after discounts and expected returns.
Include relevant COGS, shipping, fees and taxes.
Do not deduct ad spend twice.

sections.title: Use break-even as a guardrail
paragraphs: Compare it with observed ROAS over a representative window and consider conversion delay.
Pair the threshold with volume, absolute profit and attribution coverage.
bullets: Below: verify data and causes.
Above: inspect absolute profit and volume.
Recalculate after material price or cost changes.

shopifyCosts.title: Which costs should you deduct from Shopify revenue?
shopifyCosts.summary: A profit calculation is only as reliable as the cost list behind it.
shopifyCosts.answer: At minimum, reconcile revenue with product costs, shipping borne by the store, payment fees, relevant taxes, ad spend and operating expenses assigned to the period.
keyPoints: Separate variable costs, fixed costs and cash flow.
Assign each cost to the correct period and currency.
Document assumptions when data is unavailable.

sections.title: Costs tied to each order
paragraphs: Variable costs include the product, supplier shipping, packaging, shipping subsidy, payment fees and relevant taxes.
Record them by variant and transaction when possible; a global average is an assumption.
bullets: COGS by product or variant.
Shipping, packaging and transaction fees.
Discounts, returns and observed refunds.

paragraphs: Ad spend must cover the same window as sales. Add subscriptions and fixed costs for a broader operating view.
Do not confuse management reporting, cash flow and statutory accounts.
bullets: Align ads, sales and exchange rates.
Separate recurring and exceptional expenses.
Reconcile management reporting with accounting.
